Purpose: Lock character identity across images; replaces or supplements anchor weight system
Conflict detection: Conflicts with another character LoRA in same prompt → both identities merge; fix: use regional prompter or inpaint per character
Combination rules: Max 2 character LoRAs per image; 3+ requires inpaint workflow
Notes: Character LoRA + --cref not needed simultaneously; choose one method

Purpose: Control art style / brushwork / rendering quality
Conflict detection: Conflicts with realistic model checkpoint → style bleed into skin/eyes; fix: lower weight ≤0.5 or use inpaint mask
Combination rules: Stack max 2 style LoRAs; combined weight ≤1.2 total
Notes: Style LoRA does not override character features; it modifies rendering only

Conflict detection: Conflicts with scene-specific outfit prompts → outfit LoRA overrides prompt outfit; fix: lower weight or remove LoRA for that scene
Combination rules: Max 1 outfit LoRA per character; do not stack outfit LoRAs on same character
Notes: Outfit LoRA + outfit negative words = double lock; use when consistency is critical

Conflict detection: Conflicts with another concept LoRA targeting same body region → pose corruption; fix: use only 1 concept LoRA per body region
Combination rules: Stack max 2 concept LoRAs if they target different regions (e.g. pose + lighting)
Notes: Concept LoRA is scene-specific; not used across all images

Conflict detection: Conflicts with character LoRA → background bleeds into character; fix: use regional prompter or inpaint character region
Combination rules: Max 1 background LoRA; combine with character LoRA only if regional prompter available
Notes: Background LoRA weight >0.6 causes style bleed; keep ≤0.5

Purpose: Load order affects output quality — first loaded has priority
Trigger word convention: Convention: character → outfit → style → concept → background
Conflict detection: Any LoRA weight >1.0 causes artifacts; total stacked weight >2.0 causes model instability
Combination rules: Sum of all LoRA weights ≤2.0; if exceeded
column8: Priority: character > outfit > style > concept > background

Purpose: How LoRA interacts with the five-tier weight system
Trigger word convention: LoRA weight replaces numeric weight for the locked attribute; other attributes still use bracket weights
Weight range: Character LoRA = anchor (≥1.6 equivalent); style LoRA = core feature (1.3-1.5 equivalent)
Conflict detection: Conflict: anchor weight (1.8) + character LoRA (0.9) on same attribute → double-lock redundancy; fix: lower anchor weight to 1.0 and let LoRA handle identity
Combination rules: When LoRA is active: LoRA handles identity, bracket weights handle non-locked features only
Notes: LoRA does not replace negative prompts; negative words still required for trait-conflict categories

Purpose: LoRA is SD-only; MJ/Flux/GPT-4o use native reference methods
Trigger word convention: N/A — LoRA not applicable outside SD ecosystem
Conflict detection: Attempting LoRA on non-SD models = P0 failure (method mismatch)
Combination rules: For MJ use --cref; for Flux use Kontext; for GPT-4o use native reference image
Notes: Reference Image Capability Matrix governs which consistency method applies per model
